title: Kth Smallest Element in a BST
description: Given the root of a binary search tree and an integer `k`, return the `k`-th smallest value (1-indexed) among all node values in the tree.

examples.explanation: In sorted order the values are 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6.

hints: What does an in-order traversal of a BST produce?
You do not need to visit the whole tree; you can stop once you reach the k-th node in order.
Do an iterative in-order walk with a stack: push the left spine, pop a node and count it, then move to its right child. Return when the count reaches k.

solution.explanation: An in-order traversal of a BST visits values in ascending order. Simulate it iteratively with a stack: go as far left as possible pushing nodes, pop one (that is the next smallest), decrement k, and if k hits 0 return that value; otherwise continue with the popped node's right child. This costs O(h + k) time and O(h) space and stops early.
